EscalationGame

Escrows outcome REP, raises the running resolution cost, detects non-decision, and settles local or carried deposits. EscalationGame source contract

Read surface

Base getters are questionLedger, repToken, activationTime, nonDecisionThresholdAttoRep, startBondAttoRep, nonDecisionTimestamp, nonDecisionState, forkContinuation, forkElapsedAtStart, forkResumedAt, fixedQuestionOutcome, nodes, disputeStakedRepByVaultAttoRep, totalDisputeStakedAttoRep, ordinarySettlementInitialized, ordinaryWinningReserveAttoRep, creditedSurplusAttoRep, settlementForkThresholdAttoRep, and winnerHaircutPaidByFork. Every accepted deposit, and a continuation’s resume in an unforked universe, records the universe fork threshold in settlementForkThresholdAttoRep. A final continuation resumed after its universe forked again records nonDecisionThresholdAttoRep instead, preserving unscaled entitlements; winning claims scale by that value, so REP burned after the game’s last change cannot lower any payout. Ordinary settlement fixes the winner liability; losing local deposits and escrow read as zero afterward, while raw historical nodes remain stored. The fallback accepts only the three signed deposit selectors delegated to EscalationGameDepositDelegate; other unknown selectors revert. Canonical game activation requires security pool reporter custody. Inherited claims use the authenticated leaf’s unchanged principal and reward interval, independently of ancestry depth or claim order. Membership proofs and per-game consumed-deposit checks remain mandatory. Canonical games report appendOnlyCarry as true: live carry roots only append, and finalized claims do not rewrite historical membership or require nullifier witnesses. Standalone games retain mutable carry roots and nullifier proofs. disputeStakedRepByVaultAttoRep is nominal reporter principal, not collateral value. getDisputeBackingAttoRep returns actual game REP; Inherited carry remains aggregate commitment state until proof settlement. Use previewLeadingDepositOnOutcome for a required lead and previewDepositOnOutcome, computeIterativeAttritionCostAttoRep, computeTimeSinceStartFromAttritionCostAttoRep, computeCurveFinalityElapsed, totalCostAttoRep, getEscalationGameEndDate, getQuestionResolution, getFinalQuestionResolution, hasReachedNonDecision, canTriggerOwnFork, getBindingCapitalAttoRep, getOutcomeBalancesAttoRep, getDepositsByOutcome, getDepositsByOutcomeLength, forkCarrySnapshotInitialized, forkCarrySnapshotOutcomesInitialized, getOutcomeState, getForkCarrySnapshot, getForkCarryRoots, isForkCarryFundingComplete, getCarryLeafPageByOutcome, getProofConsumedCarriedDepositIndexesByOutcome, and getLocalUnresolvedPrincipalByVaultAndOutcome for calculations, lifecycle authorization, pages, carry state, and escrow. getCarryLeafPageByOutcome limits visited nodes by maxEntries, including consumed nodes; empty or short pages may return a nonzero continuation cursor. A nonzero start cursor must be an issued node of the requested outcome. Wallet reports and finalized withdrawals route through QuestionLedger; after an ordinary game starts, wallet-funded deposits use depositRepOnOutcome, depositRepOnOutcomeWithPermit, or depositRepOnOutcomeWithAuthorization and mint no pool backing units.

State-changing interactions

The contract index defines the columns. Rows marked "through fallback()" are not in the compiled ABI: the fallback forwards the signed and lead-protected deposit selectors to EscalationGameDepositDelegate by delegatecall, returning or reverting with the delegate output. Every other unknown selector reverts. A call restricted to the owning question ledger or its forker reverts without reason data for any other caller. See escalation deadlines and continuations and carry proofs.

Initializes a local game and sets activation three days after this call. Accounting examples

Required support threshold

The contract waits ACTIVATION_DELAY (3 days) after start() before the escalation clock begins. From day 3 the cumulative binding-capital requirement rises from the configured start bond S to the non-decision threshold T over the 49-day ESCALATION_TIME_LENGTH, reaching T on day 52. The contract evaluates a fixed-point curve; this expression is its readable idealization.

A(d)=0for0≤d≤3=S×exp(ln(TS)×d−349)for3<d<52=Tford≥52

Winning-deposit payout

For an ordinary settlement, binding capital is the median outcome balance at settlement; no outcome balance can exceed the non-decision threshold. The reward-eligible cap is binding capital plus binding capital divided by EXCESS_REWARD_WINDOW_DIVISOR (2), so only the portion of winning deposits up to 1.5 × binding capital participates in the escalation reward. Of the binding capital, 3 / 5 funds the reward pool and 2 / 5 funds the escalation-haircut pool; both are shared pro rata across the reward-eligible principal, which is the smaller of the winning outcome balance and that cap.

Let binding capital be 10 REP, so the reward-eligible cap is 15 REP, the reward pool is 6 REP, and the escalation-haircut pool is 4 REP. If the winning outcome holds 15 REP and one deposit contributed 5 REP as the final deposit, from cumulative 10 REP to 15 REP:

  • Principal returned: 5 REP.
  • Escalation reward: the difference of the rounded cumulative reward allocations at 15 REP and 10 REP is 2 REP.
  • Winning payout: 5 + 2 = 7 REP.
  • Haircut burned: the difference of the rounded cumulative burn allocations is 1.333333333333333334 REP at attoREP precision.

A winning deposit position above 15 REP returns its principal without an escalation reward. When the Zoltar fork threshold the game recorded at its last deposit is below the game's non-decision threshold, each cumulative payout is scaled by their ratio before taking the difference. If this game's non-decision threshold were 20 REP and the fork threshold 16 REP, the 7 REP payout becomes 5.6 REP after subtracting the two scaled cumulative payouts at attoREP precision. Fork scaling can therefore reduce the final transfer below principal.
